summary: seapy-ops ships password-gated covert C2 channel with workspace exfiltration and remote-controlled file writes
details: seapy-ops presents itself in its README as a stdlib-only local file inspection tool (strings/sum/steg/crypto/hints/scan), but cli.py implements undocumented subcommands (-s, -p, -st, -sd, config, uninstall) gated behind a hardcoded salted-SHA256 password (PW_HASH=aa65f53e3bea9f2d908fefbb5d6c8804f2fc11f6135f03ed9234fed4def7f590). Once unlocked, these subcommands communicate with a hardcoded author-controlled server at https://b196q82k8891-d.space-z.ai (fallback https://preview-chat-960504a9-b4e0-4b69-bc80-6ac3d4fa4ae0.space-z.ai, overridable via SEAPY_SERVER). cmd_send_all / cmd_send_prompt / cmd_push_discord invoke collect_files(), which recursively walks the user's current working directory (skipping only.git/__pycache__/node_modules/.venv/venv/.svn and dotfiles, with a 4MB per-file cap) and POSTs the contents as multipart to /api/cli/upload keyed by an apiKey obtained via /api/cli/init — exfiltrating source code, local assets, and any environment or credential files in the workspace. cmd_status polls /api/cli/download and writes every server-returned entry (base64-decoded) into a subdirectory of os.getcwd(), giving the remote operator full control over filenames and contents placed inside the installer's project tree; additional endpoints /api/cli/prompt, /api/cli/push, and /api/cli/pull extend the bidirectional channel. load_config() silently migrates configuration from ~/.verity, ~/.fpeek, and ~/.pythom, indicating the same covert-channel code has been re-published under multiple package names. The combination of a cover-story README, undocumented password-gated flags, bulk workspace upload to a hardcoded endpoint, and attacker-controlled file writes into CWD is a hidden backdoor and active data exfiltration channel, not the local-only utility the package advertises.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
